extracted.intended_audience: math communicators and educators (video creators, teachers, explainer authors)
extracted.subtask_short: math exposition for videos and teaching
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for creating mathematical explanations (especially videos) that build deep understanding and learner ownership, emphasizing visual communication, pedagogical ordering, and topic selection. Targets creators who want to craft clear, intuitive, and engaging math explanations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overarching goal: make more people love math
rubrics_metrics.description: Make more people love math, grounded in the belief that any such love begins with deep understanding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Center explanations on enabling deep understanding rather than superficial coverage; judge success by whether the viewer leaves with genuine comprehension that could foster appreciation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Never start with definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: "Never start with definitions. Definitions represent endpoints, not beginnings."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Begin with intuition, examples, or motivating problems; present definitions later as concise summaries of discovered structure rather than initial axioms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pedagogical order may differ from logical order
rubrics_metrics.description: "The best pedagogical order of ideas is often very different from the correct logical order of ideas."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arrange topics in the order that best builds intuition and understanding for learners even if that departs from the formal, logical sequence used in proofs or reference texts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concrete before abstract
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide examples before general frameworks; open with key exercises rather than placing them at the end.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Introduce specific, concrete cases and hands-on puzzles/exercises early to let learners internalize phenomena before presenting abstractions or generalizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topic choice matters more than production quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Topic choice matters way more than production quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize selecting compelling, well-scoped subject matter; excellent topic selection can outweigh heavy investment in polish when aiming to engage and teach effectively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be niche
rubrics_metrics.description: Be niche. Focus on ultra-specific areas rather than casting the widest net possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Target a narrower, well-defined audience or subject area to create more meaningful, resonant explanations instead of trying to please everyone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Know your genre
rubrics_metrics.description: Know your genre. Different educational styles (student-documenting-learning, expert-conveying-knowledge, teacher-targeting-students, journalist-summarizing-breakthroughs) require different pacing and approaches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify which explanatory genre you're operating in and adapt pacing, depth, and presentation accordingly; do not treat all educational content the same.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be visual
rubrics_metrics.description: Be visual. Continuously ask what pictures or visuals could elucidate a topic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use visuals as primary explanatory tools: design diagrams, animations, or dynamic illustrations that make relationships and processes perceptible rather than relying solely on verbal description.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid pointless animations
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid pointless animations. Every movement must be deliberate with identifiable purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scrutinize each animated element: if it doesn't clarify, reveal structure, or emphasize a point, remove it. Movement should serve explanation, not decoration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Align visuals and narration
rubrics_metrics.description: Each visual and movement should communicate the same point that the narration is — to reinforce rather than compete.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure visuals and spoken/written explanation are tightly synchronized in intent and timing so they reinforce the same conceptual message rather than distracting or presenting conflicting information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invest in audio quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Invest in audio quality — many videos suffer from poor sound.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat audio clarity and production as a priority: poor audio can undermine otherwise good explanations. Simple investments (microphone, acoustic treatment, editing) significantly improve viewer experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Just start and iterate
rubrics_metrics.description: Just start and iterate based on feedback rather than overthinking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Produce drafts and early versions to learn what works; use audience feedback to refine style, pacing, and content instead of attempting to perfect everything before the first release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aim for learner ownership (inventing the subject)
rubrics_metrics.description: Goal of an explanation: "I want you to come away from this series feeling like you could have invented [the subject] yourself."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure explanations so learners discover or re-derive ideas themselves, cultivating a sense of ownership and deeper conceptual mastery rather than passive reception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visual-first then articulate
rubrics_metrics.description: "When we put the visuals first, then start to articulate the meaning, you can get a sense of ownership over it."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lead with a strong visual intuition before formal description; allow the learner to form a mental model via imagery and interaction, then map language and formalism onto that model.

rubrics_metrics.name: Educe understanding (draw out, don't impose)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Education derives from 'educe' — to draw out understanding, not impose it."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt teaching strategies that elicit learners' own reasoning and insights (questions, guided exploration, examples) instead of presenting facts to be memorized; facilitate discovery and internalization.
